record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: How to decide whether a morphic word avoids (long) abelian power?

evidence.quote: How to decide whether a morphic word avoids (long) abelian power?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ (resp. $\Sigma^\omega$) the set of finite (resp. one-sided infinite) words over $\Sigma$. For a word $u\in\Sigma^*$ and a letter $a\in\Sigma$, let $|u|_a$ denote the number of occurrences of $a$ in $u$. Two finite words $u,v\in\Sigma^*$ are said to be abelian equivalent, written $u\sim_{\mathrm{ab}} v$, if $|u|=|v|$ and $|u|_a=|v|_a$ for every $a\in\Sigma$. For an integer $k\ge 2$, an abelian $k$-power is a nonempty finite word of the form $u_1u_2\cdots u_k$ with $u_1\sim_{\mathrm{ab}} u_2\sim_{\mathrm{ab}}\cdots\sim_{\mathrm{ab}} u_k$. An infinite word $w\in\Sigma^\omega$ is said to avoid abelian $k$-powers if no factor of $w$ is an abelian $k$-power, and to avoid long abelian $k$-powers if there exists $N$ such that no factor of $w$ of length at least $N$ is an abelian $k$-power.

A morphism is a map $h:\Sigma^*\to\Delta^*$ satisfying $h(uv)=h(u)h(v)$. Given an endomorphism $h:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ with a letter $a\in\Sigma$ such that $h(a)=au$ for some $u$ with $h^n(u)\ne\varepsilon$ for all $n$, the iteration produces a unique infinite fixed point $h^\omega(a)\in\Sigma^\omega$. A morphic word is the image $g(h^\omega(a))$ under a coding $g:\Sigma\to\Delta$.

Problem. Given as input a morphism $h:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$, a letter $a\in\Sigma$ generating an infinite fixed point $h^\omega(a)$, a coding $g:\Sigma\to\Delta$, and an integer $k\ge 2$, decide:
(a) whether the morphic word $g(h^\omega(a))$ avoids abelian $k$-powers;
(b) whether $g(h^\omega(a))$ avoids long abelian $k$-powers (i.e., contains only finitely many abelian $k$-power factors, equivalently has bounded-length abelian $k$-power factors).

Determine whether (a) and (b) are decidable problems in full generality, and if not, describe broad sufficient conditions on $(h,g)$ under which decidability holds.
artifact.category_tag: Combinatorics on words / abelian powers in morphic words
artifact.status_search_result: The general decision problem remains open, but partial results are known. Algorithms have been developed to decide whether the fixed point of a morphism avoids abelian k-powers under reasonable assumptions (e.g., for primitive morphisms with no eigenvalue of absolute value 1, and for certain classes of morphic and additive sequences in works by Rao, Rosenfeld, Currie and others). No fully general decision procedure for arbitrary morphic words has been established.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of Abelian Repetitions in Words (Rosenfeld thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: An algorithm is designed to decide, under reasonable assumptions, whether a morphic word avoids a pattern in the abelian sense.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability is established under sufficient conditions, not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Extending Dekking's construction of an infinite binary word avoiding abelian 4-powers
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions and verifications for specific morphic words avoiding abelian powers.
status_evidence.claim: Concrete progress on specific instances rather than a general decision procedure.

status_evidence.title: Every Binary Pattern of Length Greater Than 14 Is Abelian-2-Avoidable
status_evidence.snippet: Uses algorithmic abelian avoidance criteria to settle binary patterns.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates partial decidability tools applied to abelian avoidance.
